main.title: Space Invaders Extreme
main.summary: Space Invaders Extreme (stylized as SPACƎ INVADERS EXTRƎME) is a re-vamped incarnation of the arcade video game Space Invaders.

cards.heading: An arcade vocabulary remixed with electronic sound
cards.text: Space Invaders Extreme (stylized as SPACƎ INVADERS EXTRƎME) is a re-vamped incarnation of the arcade video game Space Invaders. The Nintendo DS and PlayStation Portable versions were released to mark the 30th anniversary of the 1978 arcade game Space Invaders. An HD version was remastered by Backbone Entertainment for Xbox Live Arcade with new four-player multiplayer modes and visualizer backgrounds by Jeff Minter, it was released on 6 May 2009 as a wrap-up to the 30th anniversary. The game is played at a fast pace with an electronic soundtrack and sound effects.

cards.heading: A second Extreme on Nintendo DS
cards.text: A sequel for the DS titled Space Invaders Extreme 2 was released in Japan on 26 March 2009, in Europe on 2 October 2009, and North America on 20 October 2009.

cards.heading: The anniversary continues on PC and consoles
cards.text: Space Invaders Extreme was released for Steam in North America on 12 February 2018 to mark the 40th anniversary of Space Invaders. It would later be released on PlayStation 4 and Nintendo Switch as part of Space Invaders Invincible Collection and Space Invaders Forever.

main.title: God of War: Chains of Olympus
main.summary: God of War: Chains of Olympus is a 2008 action-adventure game developed by Ready at Dawn, and published by Sony Computer Entertainment (SCE).

cards.heading: Kratos searches for Helios
cards.text: God of War: Chains of Olympus is a 2008 action-adventure game developed by Ready at Dawn, and published by Sony Computer Entertainment (SCE). It was first released for the PlayStation Portable (PSP) handheld console on March 4, 2008. The game is the fourth installment in the God of War series, the third chronologically, and a prequel to the original God of War. It is loosely based on Greek mythology and set in ancient Greece, with vengeance as its central motif. The player controls Kratos, a Spartan warrior who serves the Olympian gods. Kratos is guided by the goddess Athena, who instructs him to find the Sun God Helios, as the Dream God Morpheus has caused many of the gods to slumber in Helios' absence. With the power of the Sun and the aid of the Titan Atlas, Morpheus and the Queen of the Underworld Persephone intend to destroy the Pillar of the World and in turn Olympus.

cards.heading: Adapting combat to PSP
cards.text: The gameplay is similar to the previous installments, with a focus on combo-based combat, achieved through the player's main weapon—the Blades of Chaos—and secondary weapons acquired throughout the game. It features quick time events that require the player to complete game controller actions in a timed sequence to defeat stronger enemies and bosses. The player can use up to three magical attacks as alternative combat options. The game also features puzzles and platforming elements. The series' control scheme was reconfigured to compensate for the smaller number of buttons on the PSP compared to the PlayStation 2's controller; Ready at Dawn's solutions for the controls were praised by critics.

cards.heading: Reception and Origins Collection
cards.text: Chains of Olympus was acclaimed by critics, and is the highest-rated PSP title on Metacritic. As of June 2012, the game has sold 3.2 million copies worldwide, making it one of the best-selling PlayStation Portable games of all time. Together with 2010's God of War: Ghost of Sparta, Chains of Olympus was remastered and released on September 13, 2011, as part of the God of War: Origins Collection for the PlayStation 3. The remastered version was included in the God of War Saga released on August 28, 2012, also for PlayStation 3.

main.title: Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia
main.subtitle: A Ranger begins at school
main.summary: Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia is Creatures' Nintendo DS action role-playing sequel about a new recruit protecting the Almia region. The adventure begins at Ranger School before moving into professional missions and larger responsibilities. Pokémon are befriended through the Capture Styler and then provide help with obstacles or other captures. The new region includes creatures introduced in Diamond and Pearl, expanding the available partners. Beginning with training gives the familiar circling gesture a place in the story: the player learns the job alongside somebody who has only just entered it.

cards.heading: A Ranger begins at school
cards.text: Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia is Creatures' Nintendo DS action role-playing sequel about a new recruit protecting the Almia region. The adventure begins at Ranger School before moving into professional missions and larger responsibilities. Pokémon are befriended through the Capture Styler and then provide help with obstacles or other captures. The new region includes creatures introduced in Diamond and Pearl, expanding the available partners. Beginning with training gives the familiar circling gesture a place in the story: the player learns the job alongside somebody who has only just entered it.

cards.heading: Build friendship without losing the line
cards.text: Capturing now fills a Friendship Gauge through loops drawn around the target. The stylus can be lifted to avoid an attack, although a long pause allows the accumulated progress to decrease. That changes the first game's demand for an unbroken sequence into a balance between persistence and caution. The Styler also improves as the Ranger develops, making each successful loop more effective. The screen remains a small moving arena, but recognising when to interrupt a gesture is now as important as keeping the next circle accurate.

cards.heading: The right helper for the mission
cards.text: Recruited Pokémon supply the abilities needed to affect the environment and assist other captures. Their usefulness gives the player a reason to observe the area and remember which creature is nearby. Almia's larger selection broadens those opportunities without changing the basic idea of temporary cooperation. The school and subsequent assignments provide a gradual structure for that learning. Shadows of Almia builds its adventure around a form of competence different from assembling a permanent battling team: a good Ranger recognises what help is needed and knows where to find it.

main.title: Monster Hunter Freedom Unite
main.subtitle: Portable Hunting Becomes a Social Ritual
main.summary: Monster Hunter Freedom Unite makes a portable hunting party and continuity with an existing save part of its appeal.

cards.heading: Expanding Monster Hunter Freedom 2
cards.text: Monster Hunter Freedom Unite expands Monster Hunter Freedom 2 with more quests, equipment and monsters. Built for PSP, it combines an extended solo adventure with cooperative hunts for nearby players.

cards.heading: Bring the hunting party together
cards.text: Ad-hoc wireless play allowed nearby players to hunt together. Capcom emphasised this cooperative portable experience in its contemporary announcement. A difficult quarry gave the group a shared task, while the handheld hardware made meeting up with the other hunters part of arranging the session.

cards.heading: Keep the progress already made
cards.text: Save transfer from the preceding game let returning players carry progress forward rather than begin the expanded release empty-handed. By 24 April 2008, Capcom reported two million units shipped in Japan, twenty-nine days after release.

cards.heading: New quests, equipment and hunting companions
cards.text: A new Felyne companion can join solo quests. Higher-rarity armour and weapons, more equipment storage and additional ranks expand the preparations available to returning hunters. Epic Hunting Quests send several different monsters against the party in succession, while new creatures include Ukanlos.

main.title: Mario Kart Wii
main.subtitle: The Plastic Wheel That Widened the Starting Grid
main.summary: Mario Kart Wii adds motorcycles, twelve-racer events and motion steering through a Wii Remote placed inside the Wii Wheel.

cards.heading: A larger starting grid
cards.text: Mario Kart Wii debuted in Japan on April 10, 2008. The Wii Wheel places a Wii Remote inside a plastic steering-wheel shell, giving new players a familiar shape to hold. Twelve competitors share the track, with motorcycles, tricks and expanded online play joining the series' item-driven races.

cards.heading: Steering with the Wii Wheel
cards.text: The Wii Wheel adds no sensors of its own: steering comes from tilting the Wii Remote inside it. Its shape makes that movement easier to understand before the race starts. Conventional control methods remain available, letting players choose an approach that suits them.

cards.heading: Twelve racers share the track
cards.text: Twelve racers put more vehicles and items into each event. A collision or well-timed item can affect several positions as the pack moves through a corner. Players must watch nearby rivals as well as the racing line, making comebacks and sudden reversals a frequent part of the competition.

cards.heading: Motorcycles join the karts
cards.text: Motorcycles join karts for the first time in the main series. They can perform wheelies and handle differently, adding another choice alongside weight and speed before a race. Expert players explored those differences to find particularly effective combinations, extending the competition beyond simply learning each circuit.

main.title: Grand Theft Auto IV
main.subtitle: Niko Bellic arrives in Liberty City
main.summary: Grand Theft Auto IV launched simultaneously for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 on April 29, 2008 and brought the series into a denser, more physical and more melancholy Liberty City.

cards.heading: Arriving in Liberty City
cards.text: Grand Theft Auto IV launched for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 on April 29, 2008. Niko Bellic arrives in Liberty City following his cousin Roman's promises of prosperity, only to find debt and violence. Rockstar builds a denser city with heavier vehicle handling and physical reactions, while mobile-phone calls connect missions, friendships and leisure during free exploration.

cards.heading: Roman's promises and Niko's past
cards.text: Roman's stories soon give way to the difficulties of life in Liberty City. Niko brings a wartime past and tries to find a future through people whose demands keep drawing him into crime. The humour of the city's radio and advertising accompanies a more sombre story about the distance between promised success and daily survival.

cards.heading: Weight, collisions and Euphoria
cards.text: Euphoria technology contributes to the way characters react to falls and impacts. Vehicles also have pronounced suspension and inertia, making a sharp turn or collision feel different from earlier games. These changes give actions weight and unpredictability, shaping both the experience of driving and the debate around the game's handling.

cards.heading: Calls across the city
cards.text: Characters call Niko to offer work, suggest activities or ask for help. The player can accept, decline or delay while continuing to explore. Friendships therefore remain present between missions: the phone may ring during a drive or a walk through another neighbourhood. Its place within the fiction brings several activities together without leaving the city.

main.title: Ninja Gaiden II
main.subtitle: Ryu Hayabusa returns at full speed
main.summary: Ninja Gaiden II is Team Ninja's Xbox 360 action game, first released in North America on 3 June 2008. Ryu Hayabusa travels through a campaign of close combat against human and supernatural opponents, using a growing collection of weapons and ninja techniques. The sequel intensifies the speed and violence of the earlier game, asking the player to respond to several threats at once. An enemy who has been wounded can still be dangerous. Finishing an encounter therefore depends on reading what remains in front of Ryu rather than assuming an attack has settled it.

cards.heading: Ryu Hayabusa returns at full speed
cards.text: Ninja Gaiden II is Team Ninja's Xbox 360 action game, first released in North America on 3 June 2008. Ryu Hayabusa travels through a campaign of close combat against human and supernatural opponents, using a growing collection of weapons and ninja techniques. The sequel intensifies the speed and violence of the earlier game, asking the player to respond to several threats at once. An enemy who has been wounded can still be dangerous. Finishing an encounter therefore depends on reading what remains in front of Ryu rather than assuming an attack has settled it.

cards.heading: An opening can disappear quickly
cards.text: Obliteration Techniques allow Ryu to finish wounded enemies, but approaching them without care can expose him to a desperate counterattack. Blocking and evasive movement help create room for another response. Essence released during combat can restore resources or be drawn into an Ultimate Technique, giving the player a reason to decide when to collect it. Weapons such as claws, a scythe and paired swords change reach and rhythm. The challenge comes from connecting these actions under pressure, turning a brief opening into a controlled attack before another opponent interrupts.

cards.heading: Survive the encounter, then recover
cards.text: Health partly recovers after a fight, while lasting damage limits how much returns without an item or a save statue. This structure encourages the player to finish a dangerous exchange, then consider what has been lost before continuing. The game was Tomonobu Itagaki's final directed release before leaving Tecmo. Ninja Gaiden Sigma 2 followed on PlayStation 3 in 2009 with substantial changes, and Ninja Gaiden 2 Black revisited the game in 2025. The original Xbox 360 version retains its own balance, enemy pressure and distinctive combat pace.

main.title: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots
main.summary: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots is a 2008 action-adventure stealth game developed by Kojima Productions and published by Konami for the PlayStation 3.

cards.heading: Old Snake's final mission
cards.text: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots is a 2008 action-adventure stealth game developed by Kojima Productions and published by Konami for the PlayStation 3. Directed, written, and designed by series creator Hideo Kojima, it is the sixth mainline Metal Gear game and a narrative sequel to Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty (2001). Set five years after the events of Sons of Liberty, the story centers around a rapidly aging Solid Snake, now known as Old Snake, as he goes on one last mission to assassinate Liquid Ocelot, the body of Revolver Ocelot inhabited by Liquid Snake, before he takes control of the Sons of the Patriots, an A.I. system that controls the activities of PMCs worldwide.

cards.heading: Reception and the continuing series
cards.text: Guns of the Patriots won several Game of the Year awards and sold six million copies worldwide by 2014. Critics praised its combat, graphics, characters and emotional weight, while some found the plot convoluted and the cutscenes excessive. Peace Walker followed in 2010, and Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance explored events after Guns of the Patriots in 2013.

main.title: Guitar Hero: Aerosmith
main.subtitle: A career told through the setlist
main.summary: Aerosmith’s music, venues and digital band members turn Guitar Hero into a playable band retrospective.

cards.heading: From opening act to headliner
cards.text: Guitar Hero: Aerosmith makes one band the organising principle of an entire game. Its career moves through six tiers associated with stages in Aerosmith’s history. Songs by opening acts introduce each section before the player takes on the band’s own repertoire. The underlying guitar play comes from Guitar Hero III, with fret patterns, strumming and Star Power, rather than the four-instrument ensemble introduced by World Tour.

cards.heading: Recreating a band
cards.text: The band contributed motion capture so that its members could appear as recognisable performers on the virtual stage. The soundtrack combines Aerosmith recordings with music by other acts, and several early Aerosmith songs were re-recorded for the project. Venues and contextual material make the career more than a list of unrelated challenges, although reviewers also questioned the shorter, generally easier selection. The original console release was followed by a computer edition later in 2008.

main.title: Trauma Center: Under the Knife 2
main.subtitle: Derek returns to the operating table
main.summary: Trauma Center: Under the Knife 2 is Vanguard and Atlus' Nintendo DS surgical thriller continuing the story of Derek Stiles three years after the first game. The return of the GUILT disease draws him back into dangerous medical work, alongside the personal uncertainty and institutional pressures surrounding his profession. Story scenes lead into operations performed with the stylus, retaining the original handheld arrangement. The sequel returns to the same surgeon and working surface, allowing the player's familiarity with his instruments to meet a new sequence of patients and emergencies.

cards.heading: Derek returns to the operating table
cards.text: Trauma Center: Under the Knife 2 is Vanguard and Atlus' Nintendo DS surgical thriller continuing the story of Derek Stiles three years after the first game. The return of the GUILT disease draws him back into dangerous medical work, alongside the personal uncertainty and institutional pressures surrounding his profession. Story scenes lead into operations performed with the stylus, retaining the original handheld arrangement. The sequel returns to the same surgeon and working surface, allowing the player's familiarity with his instruments to meet a new sequence of patients and emergencies.

cards.heading: A steady hand needs a clear sequence
cards.text: The available instruments include a scalpel, laser, ultrasound and defibrillator, each selected from icons around the touchscreen. Treating a patient may require dealing with surface wounds and internal injuries while watching the time limit and vital signs. Antibiotic gel and other support tools help maintain the condition needed to complete the procedure. Different difficulty settings provide another way into the demanding sequences. The work still depends on recognising which problem should be treated next, then carrying out the appropriate movement without allowing another urgent condition to become unmanageable.

cards.heading: An impossible disease creates an unusual operation
cards.text: GUILT strains turn selected procedures into confrontations with an artificial threat inside the patient. Derek's Healing Touch remains available when the situation calls for his exceptional ability, connecting a supernatural story element with the timing of the player's actions. Portraits and conversations give the medical team space between those emergencies. Under the Knife 2 builds on an already recognisable set of tools, using the continuing story to give another operation a different context and another reason to care about completing the procedure before the patient's condition becomes critical.
